---
title: Skills & skill frames
description: A skill is a named multi-step flow the planner commits to; the frame narrows the served space to the skill's steps plus a guaranteed escape.
---

A **skill** is a named multi-step flow: `does` (the planner text), `steps` (tool ids by
qualified path or unambiguous suffix, resolved loudly at build time), and an optional `when`
precondition. Skills are what [Mode B serves as fixed tools](doc:modes) — one tool per skill,
forever.

## Frames — on-demand disclosure

Opening a skill (`commitSkill`, or calling its Mode B tool with no `step`) opens a **frame**:
the served action space narrows to the frame's steps plus authored cancel/back plus the
synthetic **leave-skill escape** — guaranteed for every frame that opens, so a committed
planner is never locked in. The frame's result discloses `readySteps` (fireable now),
`laterSteps` (with status), and `awaitingState` (steps whose fire has not yet been reported
back — see [the settlement rule](doc:sessions#the-settlement-rule)).

`skillPlan(id)` returns the derived dependency DAG with live per-step status — and THROWS on
an unknown id, because every in-library caller passes an id the spec just yielded.
`trySkillPlan(id)` is the same plan for an id you did **not** author (a model's, a URL's):
`{ ok: true, plan }` or `{ ok: false, reason: 'UNKNOWN_SKILL', known }` — the identical
failure shape `commitSkill()` returns, so a caller holding a model-supplied id handles the
question one way.

## The commit gates — five typed refusals

`commitSkill()` refuses, in order, with a typed reason:

1. `UNKNOWN_SKILL` — with `known`, the list of real ids;
2. `STALE_CURSOR` — the world moved since the caller looked;
3. `FRAME_ALREADY_OPEN` — one committed flow at a time;
4. `PRECONDITION_FAILED` — the skill's `when` fails against projected state;
5. `ENTRY_NOT_MATERIALIZED` — **the never-trap gate.** An agent commit outside a tour
   session is refused when the entry step could not act AT ALL right now: no registered
   handler under any key (instance-keyed wiring on a repeats container counts — the fire
   that follows carries the instance) and no navigate-derived gesture. The refusal carries
   the entry step's `affordanceId` and, when declared, its `gesture`. The frame that could
   never act is never opened.

The fifth gate asks the **same widened materialisation question** `fire()` asks — one code
path, never a second lookup — so the commit gate and the fire gate can never disagree. See
[Actuation &amp; materialisation](doc:actuation#the-never-trap-invariant).

If your agent flow commits skills before the app's handlers mount: register the entry step's
handler first (the same wiring 0.3.0 asked of fires), pass the `navigate` option when the
entry is a pure navigation, commit with `source: 'user'` for human-driven flows, or create
the session with `allowUnmaterializedFires` for touring.

Only the `ENTRY_NOT_MATERIALIZED` refusal lands a [gap-ledger](doc:sessions#the-gap-ledger)
row — it is a capability gap (a binding to build). The other four are protocol events, not
capability gaps, and stay un-ledgered.

## Journeys are skills

If your app already owns journey definitions, [`fromJourneys`](doc:graph-sources) reads them
as skills in the same `does` / `steps` / `when` vocabulary — one authoring language, compiled
by the same skills pass, refused in the same voice.
